newsitem.title: USA: Motorola sees 400 mln wireless phone users by 2000.
newsitem.headline: Motorola sees 400 mln wireless phone users by 2000.

text.p: Motorola Inc said Thursday it sees the number of wireless telephone users worldwide hitting 400 million by the year 2000 after growing some 41 percent in just the last year.

At its annual analysts' meeting, the technology giant said the number of cellular and PCS (personal communications services) subscribers reached more than 160 million in June, 1997 -- up from 108 million in June, 1996.

"We believe the industry is on the way to meeting or exceeding our projection of the worldwide cellular/PCS subscriber base reaching 400 million by the year 2000," Bob Weisshappel, president and general manager of Motorola's Cellular Subscriber Sector, said.
The industry remains extremely competitive as wireless networks are upgraded to digital from analog, and phone prices continue to fall. But Weisshappel said his sector remains solidly profitable.
"This is the environment that we've learned not only to survive in but thrive in," he added.

In addition, the Schaumburg, Ill.-based company has various new digital phones currently in field trials and ready for release. Motorola was late to market with Global System for Mobile communications (GSM) phones, but has since launched several new products and said its market share is growing. GSM, used widely in Europe, accounts for more than 75 percent of the world digital wireless phone market, the company said.
"We have now created an extremely strong product combination in this area (GSM) after admittedly a difficult year last year," Weisshappel said.

Weisshappel said the company is dealing with eroding prices by focusing on mid- and high-tier products, which in addition to creating value in the market have higher margins. One example is the StarTAC phone, which is about the size of a pager and is very light.
Plus Motorola is relying on its years of experience.
"Those two things will yield a very, very good business," he said.
